verdict.summary: Composio has no managed Shopify app, so you have to register your own. Creating it in the Dev Dashboard and installing it on your own development store is self-serve and quick. Going public is the hard part: public apps need a review to get protected customer data (customer name, email, address, phone) and a separate App Store review to be listed. Shopify publishes no timeline for either.
verdict.hands_on_effort: About 1 hour to reach your own dev store. 1-3+ days to prepare the protected-data request, data-security controls, compliance webhooks and App Store listing.
verdict.approval_wait: Unknown. Shopify publishes no timeline for protected customer data or App Store review.

steps.title: Get a Shopify account with app development permissions
steps.detail: Create a free Shopify Partner account (or sign in to one), and make sure your user has app development permissions. Create a development store to test on.

steps.title: Create the app in the Dev Dashboard
steps.detail: In the Dev Dashboard, go to Apps > Create app > Start from Dev Dashboard and enter an app name.
gotchas: If you plan to list the app later, leave the word "Shopify" (and misspellings or abbreviations of it) out of the app name, URLs and contact emails.

steps.title: Choose a minimal scope list
steps.detail: Composio's default list has 36 scopes, many of them write scopes. Keep only the scopes your agent actually uses. Shopify approves protected customer data only when you request the minimum needed, and merchants have to re-approve any scopes you add later.

steps.title: Create and release an app version with the redirect URL and scopes
steps.detail: In the Dev Dashboard, open your app's Versions page and click Create version. Enter the allowed redirection URL and your scopes, then release the version. The app can't be installed until a version exists.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Redirect URLs now live under Versions in the Dev Dashboard, not in the old Partner Dashboard location.
If the URL doesn't exactly match the one Composio sends, OAuth fails with 'The redirect_uri is not whitelisted'.

steps.title: Copy the Client ID and secret into Composio
steps.detail: In the Dev Dashboard, open your app and go to App settings. Copy the Client ID and Client secret into a Composio Shopify auth config that uses your own OAuth app, and enter the same scopes as your app version.

steps.title: Install on your development store and test authorization
steps.detail: Start a Composio connection for your development store's subdomain. This sends you to {subdomain}.myshopify.com/admin/oauth/authorize. Approve the scopes and make a test Admin API call.
gotchas: Authorization works per store, so the connection needs the store subdomain.
A wrong client_id doesn't return a normal OAuth error: Shopify shows a 403 'Verifying your connection' page instead.

steps.title: Select a distribution method
steps.detail: Choose custom or public distribution. You have to do this before you can request protected customer data, even on development stores. Custom apps get Level 1 and Level 2 data without review. Public apps need review.

steps.title: Request protected customer data access (public apps)
steps.detail: Draft a reason for each protected field you need (name, email, address and phone are requested separately), then submit the request in the Partner Dashboard. Level 2 covers those four fields. Shopify redacts any field it doesn't approve.
gotchas: You can't submit this request while the app is under App Store review, so do it before or after.

steps.title: Put the Level 1/2 data-protection controls in place
steps.detail: Put the required controls in place: encrypted backups, separate test and production data, access logs, and a security incident response policy. Shopify may request a data protection review later, most likely for apps with many installs, many customer records or many approved fields.

steps.title: Switch to expiring offline tokens
steps.detail: Since April 1, 2026, new public apps must use expiring offline tokens: 60-minute access tokens plus refresh tokens that last up to 90 days. Every refresh returns a new refresh token, and you must store it. Check that your Composio setup handles this rotation.
gotchas: Only one refreshable expiring offline token exists per app and store.
Existing public apps must stop using non-expiring offline tokens by January 1, 2027.

steps.title: Prepare the App Store submission materials
steps.detail: Subscribe to the compliance webhooks. Prepare a 1200x1200 JPEG or PNG icon, choose a primary language and write at least one listing. Add an emergency developer email and phone number.

steps.title: Submit for App Store review
steps.detail: Fill in the required fields on the App Store review page, pass the automated checks and submit.

steps.title: Wait for review and answer reviewer emails
steps.detail: Reply to reviewer emails promptly and fix every issue they raise. Ignored emails or repeated failures can trigger resubmission cooldowns, and each cooldown is longer than the last.

scopes.effect: Customer data is protected customer data. Public apps need review for Level 1, and for Level 2, which adds name, address, phone and email. Custom apps get both levels without review.

scopes.scope: Composio default list (36 scopes, many write)
scopes.effect: Request only what you use. Shopify wants the minimum for protected data approval, and merchants have to manually approve any scopes you add later.

blockers.cause: The redirect URI Composio sends isn't in the released app version's allowed redirection URLs.
blockers.fix: Create a new version under Versions in the Dev Dashboard with the exact Composio callback URL, then release it.

blockers.symptom: 403 'Verifying your connection' page instead of the consent screen
blockers.cause: Seen when the client_id is invalid. Shopify doesn't return standard OAuth error parameters.
blockers.fix: Re-copy the Client ID from App settings and confirm the store subdomain is correct.

blockers.symptom: App Store submission rejected over the name, URL or email
blockers.cause: The app name, URLs or contact emails contain 'Shopify' (or a misspelling or abbreviation of it) or 'Example'.
blockers.fix: Rename the app and use different URLs and emails before you submit.

blockers.cause: A cooldown period after repeated unresolved issues or unanswered review emails.
blockers.fix: Answer reviewer emails quickly and fix all issues before you resubmit.

blockers.cause: No distribution method is selected yet, or the app is currently under App Store review.
blockers.fix: Select a distribution method first, and submit the data request outside the App Store review window.

blockers.cause: Shopify hasn't approved those protected fields.
blockers.fix: Request each field with a reason and keep the request to the minimum you need.

composio.note: Composio has no managed OAuth app for Shopify, so you have to register your own app in the Dev Dashboard and give Composio its Client ID and secret. Composio uses per-store URLs: https://{subdomain}.myshopify.com/admin/oauth/authorize and /admin/oauth/access_token. Composio's default redirect is https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add, but a v3 callback was also seen, so copy the exact callback URL from your Composio auth config into your app version's redirection URLs. Cut the long default scope list down to what you use.

evidence.quote: you'll need to request access to the following protected customer fields individually

evidence.claim: Shopify approves protected customer data only if the requested data is the minimum the app needs; unapproved fields are redacted.
evidence.quote: Shopify will approve your app to use protected customer data if the requested data is the minimum amount required

evidence.claim: Apps installed only on development stores can access customer data in development without submitting a review request.
evidence.quote: You don't need to submit a request for review for apps that are installed only on development stores.

evidence.claim: Level 2 apps must meet level 1 and 2 requirements, including encrypted backups, separate test and production data, access logs, and an incident response policy.
evidence.quote: Implement a security incident response policy.

evidence.claim: A data protection review may be requested after implementation, most likely for apps with high install counts, many customer records, or many approved fields.
evidence.quote: While any app might be selected, data protection reviews will likely focus on apps that have

evidence.claim: Applying for protected customer data is not possible while the app is under review.
evidence.quote: Applying for protected customer data isn't possible while the app is under review.

evidence.claim: App Store submission goes through the App Store review page with mandatory fields, automated checks, a primary language, and at least one listing.
evidence.quote: Every app submission must specify a primary language and create at least one Shopify App Store listing.

evidence.claim: Public apps listed in the App Store must subscribe to compliance webhooks.
evidence.quote: Apps that are distributed through the Shopify App Store must subscribe to compliance webhooks.

evidence.claim: App icon must be 1200 x 1200 pixels in JPEG or PNG format.
evidence.quote: must be 1200 x 1200 pixels in size and in either JPEG or PNG format.

evidence.claim: Common rejection cause: app URLs, contact emails, or names with the word Shopify or misspellings/abbreviations of it are not permitted.
evidence.quote: make sure you don't include the words "Shopify" or "Example".

evidence.claim: Partners can enter a temporary cooldown that blocks resubmission, for example after repeatedly failing to address reviewer issues or not responding to review emails; repeated cooldowns get longer.
evidence.quote: If your app repeatedly enters a cooldown period, then later cooldown periods are longer.

evidence.claim: Emergency developer contact email and phone number are required for critical technical issues.
evidence.quote: You need to provide an email and phone number in case critical technical issues with your app arise

evidence.claim: OAuth authorization is per store: the merchant is sent to the store's admin authorize URL with client_id, redirect_uri and scope; the redirect URI must be set by the developer in the request.
evidence.quote: there isn't a default value for the URI redirect field

evidence.claim: Whitelisted redirection URLs are set per app version in the Dev Dashboard (Versions > Create version); the older Partner Dashboard location has moved and is reported as confusing.
evidence.quote: under the app developer dashboard(portal) there is version

evidence.claim: A redirect_uri not on the allowed list causes an invalid_request error ('redirect_uri is not whitelisted') during OAuth.
evidence.quote: The redirect_uri is not whitelisted

evidence.claim: Admin-API access tokens: online tokens expire after 24 hours; client credentials tokens from a dev-dashboard app expire after 24 hours; public apps using client assertions get up to 1 hour.
evidence.quote: An online token expires after 24 hours or when the user logs out of the Shopify admin

evidence.claim: Since April 1, 2026 all new public apps must use expiring offline access tokens (60-minute access tokens with refresh tokens).
evidence.quote: all new public apps must request and use expiring offline access tokens.

evidence.claim: Refresh tokens for expiring offline tokens last 90 days when issued, and using them to refresh can shorten that lifetime.
evidence.quote: 90 days (refresh_token_expires_in is 7776000) when issued.

evidence.claim: Each refresh rotates tokens: the app receives a new refresh token and must store it, and only one refreshable expiring offline token exists per app and store.
evidence.quote: only one refreshable expiring offline token exists per app+store

evidence.claim: Existing public apps must move off non-expiring offline tokens by January 1, 2027.
evidence.quote: existing public apps can't after January 1, 2027.

evidence.claim: Free Shopify Partner account and a development store are commonly listed prerequisites for building an app (community sources).
evidence.quote: A Shopify Partner account (free to create at partners.shopify.com)

evidence.claim: The Shopify authorize endpoint responded to a deliberately invalid client_id by redirecting to admin.shopify.com with a 403 'Verifying your connection' page, with no standard OAuth error parameters returned.
evidence.quote: Verifying your connection... Your connection needs to be verified before you can proceed

open_questions: Shopify publishes no official timeline for App Store review or protected customer data review.
Not confirmed which Composio redirect must be allowlisted: backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add or the v3 callback. Copy it from your Composio auth config.
Not confirmed whether a public app can be installed by any merchant without App Store review (an unlisted public app), or only after listing review.
Install caps for custom-distribution and unreviewed apps were not found.
Not confirmed whether Composio's Shopify integration handles expiring offline tokens with rotating refresh tokens, which new public apps must use.
The Dev Dashboard returned HTTP 406 to the probe, so the UI steps come from the docs and were not checked against the live console.
The exact compliance webhook topics were not fetched from an official page.
PKCE support and the full list of sensitive scopes beyond protected customer data were not confirmed.
Sources disagree on whether redirect URLs live in the Partner Dashboard or the Dev Dashboard. The official docs place them under Versions in the Dev Dashboard.
